title: Quarterly trajectory scratchpad — Vela Martinez
content:
Quarterly trajectory + manager prep: raw brain-dump and examples

Context (short):
I run the onboarding and early-stage hiring funnel for people-ops, plus a small programs scope (internship, grad hiring pilots). In the last quarter I leaned into cross-functional onboarding improvements and reduced time-to-first-success for new ICs. This doc is my prep for the upcoming 1:1 + my own self-eval notes for Q4->Q1 transition.

Quick wins to call out (evidence + where to find it):
- Reduced new-hire SysOps onboarding time from 6.5 -> 4.2 weeks (measured by first successful oncall handover). Data: onboarding-dashboard row 12, cohort Sep->Dec. Metric tracked in sheet "onboard-metrics-2025".
- Piloted buddy-checklist for SWE interns; average satisfaction on post-30-day survey = 4.4/5 (n=12). Saved ~8 hours per hiring manager in ramp tasks. Link: Confluence pilot notes (linked above).
- Launched weekly onboarding drop-in AMA (15–25 attendees) that cut re-opened access tickets by ~30%. Slack thread ID: (see linked_artifacts).

Areas I own that need attention (what I'll say + plan):
1) Hiring velocity for mid/Sr IC roles is slipping (pipeline -> offer conversion).
   - Evidence: JIRA-OPS-3421 recruiter funnel report, avg time-to-offer increased from 21 -> 33 days.
   - Why I care: impacts roadmap delivery and budget for Dedicated team hires next quarter.
   - Plan: partner with recruiting to run a one-week "fast-track" cohort for high-priority reqs; propose experiment and metrics (time-to-screen, interviewer acceptance rates). Draft experiment brief: due Mar 10.

2) Onboarding knowledge fragmentation across teams.
   - Symptoms: repeated ticket categories; duplicate runbooks; inconsistent first-week checklists.
   - Micro-actions: (a) consolidate top-6 runbooks into canonical "start-here" playbook; (b) standardize Day-0 checklist template and enforce in hiring-offer cadence.
   - Quick ask for manager: time to reallocate 4 hours from my capacity for doc sprint next week (blocking: need reviewer 1 from infra).

Signals of progress to track (for my 90-day goals):
- Metric A: time-to-first-success (weeks) median per cohort (goal: <= 4 weeks for engineers).
- Metric B: new-hire NPS (30-day) target >= 4.2.
- Metric C: reopened onboarding tickets per cohort <= 15.
- Soft signal: hiring manager satisfaction comment examples (collect 3 quotes per month).

Concrete 90-day goals (draft language for performance doc):
- Goal 1 (impact): Decrease median time-to-first-success for new engineering hires from 5.1 to <= 4.0 weeks by shipping a standardized Day-0/Week-1 playbook and running two onboarding pilots.
  - Why it matters: improves new hire productivity and reduces manager time spent on basic ramp tasks.
  - Measurement: onboarding-dashboard and post-30-day survey.

- Goal 2 (process): Improve mid/Sr hiring pipeline conversion by implementing a fast-track experiment for 5 high-priority roles and improving recruiter-interviewer alignment.
  - Measurement: avg time-to-offer, interview no-show rate, offer acceptance rate.

- Goal 3 (leadership): Create a repeatable "internship to hire" pathway and present results to Hiring Council by end of quarter.
  - Measurement: conversion rate of interns to full-time, qualitative manager readiness.

Anecdotes / examples to use in self-eval:
- Story 1: During the Oct cohort we had a critical access failure for a new hire. I triaged with infra, created a temporary sandbox, and documented the fix as a runbook that prevented recurrence. (Shows bias for action + cross-team ops).
- Story 2: The buddy-checklist pilot surfaced an unexpected content gap in our infra orientation. I partnered with infra doc owner and we shipped a 20-min recorded walkthrough for new hires (immediate drop in support questions).

Manager prep: items to discuss in 1:1
- Headcount ask: propose re-prioritizing 0.3 FTE from org enablement to onboarding enablement for next quarter to support playbook rollout.
- Support needed: review and signoff for the fast-track experiment brief (I need decision by Mar 15).
- Feedback request: clarity on promotion track timing — can I push for IC2 -> IC3 consideration based on outcomes? Prepare concrete evidence (metrics and stories above).

Open questions / risks (notes to self):
- Risk: Hiring market volatility may make fast-track cause quality regressions. Mitigation: include a 2-week quality gate and sample code challenge retention check.
- Unknown: whether legal/compliance needs review for the new intern pathway (need to ping legal).
- Data gap: we don't have clean cohort-level time-to-first-success for contractors (ask analytics for cohort tagging).

Action items (next 14 days):
- Draft fast-track experiment brief + metrics (due Mar 10).
- Doc sprint for canonical runbooks (book reviewer from infra; ask Amelie).
- Pull onboarding-dashboard export and prepare 1-page for manager meeting (include 3 exemplar quotes).
- Ping legal about intern pathway (Noah to intro).

Snippets for self-eval (one-liners I can drop into doc):
- "Led the consolidation of onboarding runbooks and launched two pilots that reduced median time-to-first-success by ~1.3 weeks for engineer cohorts."
- "Designed and ran a buddy-checklist pilot that improved 30-day new-hire NPS to 4.4/5 and reduced reopened tickets by 30%."

Notes-to-self style reminders: keep examples metric-forward, avoid listing too many small tasks, emphasize scalability (how my work prevents 1:1 fixes), and surface 2~3 tradeoffs I made.

Misc scratch (questions I might ask manager):
- "If I can free 0.3 FTE from org enablement, can we treat this as a temporary shift for quarter X to get playbooks off the ground?"
- "What are the signal thresholds you’d want to see to approve IC level progression?"

End of scratchpad. Will prune and move selected lines into the formal self-eval doc next week.
